description: Curated structural knowledge graph of hazard -> system disruption and system -> system propagation. Reference-class knowledge (scientific literature and official open data practice), NOT a loss model. Used by src/climate/cascading.py to select cascade paths relevant to a location's REAL active hazards and REAL mapped exposure anchors.
not_quantified_statement: Propagation likelihoods and losses are NOT quantified — this is a structural relevance graph, not a loss model.
evidence_note: Every edge carries an evidence_class plus an evidence block: class (SCIENTIFIC — mechanism established in the scientific literature, e.g. IPCC AR6 WG2 compound/cascading risk chapters, or OPEN_DATA_OFFICIAL — dependency documented in official/open-data infrastructure practice), basis (one line naming the documented mechanism class — reference CLASSES, not fabricated citations), confidence (high|medium|low) and limitations (one line). quantified is always false: no edge carries a likelihood or loss figure.

edges.mechanism: Flame, heat and smoke damage lines and substations; operators may pre-emptively de-energise lines in high fire danger.

evidence.basis: Wildfire–power infrastructure interaction documented by fire agencies and grid-operator wildfire-mitigation guidance (incl. public-safety power shutoff practice).
evidence.limitations: Line exposure and shutoff policy are operator- and terrain-specific.

edges.mechanism: Fire, smoke and falling debris force road closures and can cut evacuation routes.

evidence.basis: Wildfire road-closure and evacuation-route impacts documented in post-fire agency situation reports and emergency-management guidance.
evidence.limitations: Closure extent and duration are event-specific.

edges.mechanism: Flames and heat destroy crops, pasture and livestock; smoke taints produce.

evidence.basis: Fire and smoke damage to crops, pasture and livestock established in the agricultural loss-assessment literature.
evidence.limitations: Severity depends on season, crop stage and fire behaviour.

edges.mechanism: Fire danger and smoke close natural areas and deter visitors.

evidence.basis: Wildfire-driven area closures and visitor deterrence documented in protected-area management and tourism-impact assessments.
evidence.limitations: Demand effects are season- and destination-dependent.

edges.mechanism: Floodwater inundates and erodes road surfaces, cutting road links.

evidence.basis: Flood inundation and erosion of road infrastructure established in flood-risk and post-event damage-assessment literature.
evidence.limitations: Tolerable depth/duration varies by road design and drainage.

edges.mechanism: Floodwater undermines track beds and bridges, closing lines.

evidence.basis: Flood damage to track beds and bridges documented by railway infrastructure managers and post-flood engineering assessments.
evidence.limitations: Line-specific engineering and drainage determine tolerance.

edges.mechanism: Flooding damages intake and treatment infrastructure and contaminates supplies.

evidence.basis: Flood damage and contamination of water intake and treatment established in water-utility flood-resilience guidance.
evidence.limitations: Treatment redundancy and source protection differ by utility.

edges.mechanism: Inundation damages facilities and blocks patient and staff access.

evidence.basis: Flood impacts on healthcare facilities and access documented in hospital emergency-planning and post-event assessment literature.
evidence.limitations: Facility elevation, flood protection and preparedness vary widely.

edges.mechanism: Prolonged inundation waterlogs crops and erodes topsoil.

evidence.basis: Crop waterlogging and topsoil erosion under prolonged inundation established in agricultural flood-impact literature.
evidence.limitations: Tolerance depends on crop type, growth stage and duration.

edges.mechanism: Inundation damages industrial sites and forces shutdowns.

evidence.basis: Industrial-site flood damage and forced shutdowns documented in post-event damage surveys.
evidence.limitations: Site-level protection and process criticality are heterogeneous.

edges.mechanism: Extended precipitation deficit depletes reservoirs and groundwater, constraining supply.

evidence.basis: Drought depletion of reservoirs and groundwater constraining supply established in drought-management and water-resources literature.
evidence.limitations: Storage buffer and demand management differ by utility.

edges.mechanism: Soil-moisture deficit stresses rain-fed crops and pasture.

evidence.basis: Soil-moisture deficit stress on rain-fed crops and pasture established in the agricultural drought literature.
evidence.limitations: Irrigation access strongly modulates the impact.

edges.mechanism: Low reservoir levels and warm rivers constrain hydropower and thermal-plant cooling.

evidence.basis: Hydropower and thermal-cooling constraints under low flow and high water temperature documented in energy-sector drought assessments.
evidence.limitations: The generation mix determines how exposed a grid is.

edges.mechanism: Peak cooling demand rises while lines and transformers derate in high temperatures.

evidence.basis: Heat-driven demand peaks and equipment derating documented in grid-operator summer-readiness practice and power-sector heat literature.
evidence.limitations: Derating curves and demand response are asset- and market-specific.

edges.mechanism: Heat illness raises admissions, stressing emergency care.

evidence.basis: Heat-related morbidity raising admissions established in the heatwave–health impact literature.
evidence.limitations: Vulnerability varies with demographics, housing and adaptation.

edges.mechanism: Rail buckling risk rises in extreme heat, forcing speed restrictions and closures.

evidence.basis: Rail buckling risk and heat speed restrictions documented by railway infrastructure managers.
evidence.limitations: Critical rail temperatures differ by track maintenance standard.

edges.mechanism: Heat forces closures or degraded conditions in non-cooled school buildings.

evidence.basis: Heat-driven school closures and degraded learning conditions documented in public-health and education-facility guidance.
evidence.limitations: Cooling availability varies by building stock and policy.

edges.mechanism: Heat stress cuts yields and raises livestock mortality risk.

evidence.basis: Heat-stress impacts on crop yields and livestock established in the agricultural heat-stress literature.
evidence.limitations: Thermal thresholds are species- and variety-specific.

edges.mechanism: Windthrow of trees and poles and line galloping cause outages.

evidence.basis: Windthrow and line damage causing outages documented in storm-impact research and grid-operator post-storm reports.
evidence.limitations: Forest proximity and network vintage strongly modulate damage.

edges.mechanism: Fallen trees and debris block roads; high-profile vehicles are restricted.

evidence.basis: Storm-debris road closures and high-profile-vehicle restrictions documented in road-authority incident and severe-weather practice.
evidence.limitations: Closure decisions are authority- and event-specific.

edges.mechanism: Wind damages overhead telecom lines and mast infrastructure, degrading coverage.

evidence.basis: Wind damage to overhead telecom lines and masts documented in operator resilience guidance and post-storm service reports.
evidence.limitations: Buried versus overhead plant changes exposure substantially.

edges.mechanism: Extreme still-water levels and waves disrupt port operations and damage quays.

evidence.basis: Extreme water levels and wave action disrupting port operations documented in port climate-adaptation literature.
evidence.limitations: Design still-water levels and downtime thresholds differ by port.

edges.mechanism: Coastal flooding and erosion cut coastal roads.

evidence.basis: Coastal flooding and erosion cutting coastal roads documented in coastal-risk and shoreline-management assessments.
evidence.limitations: Defence standards vary along the coast.

edges.mechanism: Beach erosion and coastal flooding degrade tourism assets.

evidence.basis: Beach erosion and coastal-flood damage to tourism assets documented in coastal tourism-risk literature.
evidence.limitations: Seasonal demand and nourishment practice modulate impacts.

edges.mechanism: Outages force hospitals onto backup power; prolonged loss degrades care.

evidence.basis: Hospital dependence on backup power during outages documented in health-facility emergency-management standards.
evidence.limitations: Backup autonomy and fuel supply vary by facility.

edges.mechanism: Pumping and treatment depend on power; outages interrupt supply.

evidence.basis: Power dependence of water pumping and treatment documented in water-utility resilience and emergency-planning guidance.
evidence.limitations: On-site generation and storage differ by utility.

edges.mechanism: Towers and exchanges have limited battery backup; outages degrade networks.

evidence.basis: Limited battery backup at towers and exchanges documented in telecom resilience regulation and operator disclosure.
evidence.limitations: Backup duration varies widely by site and operator.

edges.mechanism: Electrified lines and signalling stop without power.

evidence.basis: Power dependence of electrified rail and signalling documented by railway infrastructure operators.
evidence.limitations: Diesel fallback exists only on parts of some networks.

edges.mechanism: Outages halt trading, cold chains and production.

evidence.basis: Outage impacts on trading, cold chains and production documented in business-continuity management standards practice.
evidence.limitations: Firm-level backup and tolerance vary widely.

edges.mechanism: Water loss interrupts sanitation, sterilisation and cooling; hospitals cannot operate safely without supply.

evidence.basis: Hospital water dependence documented in health-facility water-safety planning guidance.
evidence.limitations: On-site storage capacity varies by facility.

edges.mechanism: Irrigation draws on supplies that are constrained in drought.

evidence.basis: Irrigation reliance on supplies constrained in drought established in the agricultural water-use literature.
evidence.limitations: Water rights, storage and conveyance modulate the constraint.

edges.mechanism: Road closures reroute and delay freight.

evidence.basis: Road-closure rerouting and freight delay documented in freight and road-authority incident-management practice.
evidence.limitations: Network redundancy varies regionally.

edges.mechanism: Rail closures shift freight onto constrained road capacity.

evidence.basis: Rail-freight diversion onto road capacity documented in freight modal-shift practice.
evidence.limitations: Modal substitutability is commodity- and corridor-specific.

edges.mechanism: Port disruption breaks import and export chains.

evidence.basis: Port disruption breaking import/export chains documented in supply-chain resilience practice.
evidence.limitations: Alternative port capacity and hinterland links vary.

edges.mechanism: Supply delays halt production and retail.

evidence.basis: Supply-delay propagation to production and retail documented in supply-chain risk-management practice.
evidence.limitations: Inventory buffers and dual sourcing differ by firm.

edges.mechanism: Loss of communications disrupts payments, coordination and remote work.

evidence.basis: Communications loss disrupting payments and coordination documented in business-continuity management practice.
evidence.limitations: Digital dependence varies by sector.

edges.mechanism: Crop losses propagate to food processing and farm income.

evidence.basis: Crop-loss propagation to food processing and farm income established in the agricultural economics literature.
evidence.limitations: Market substitution and insurance can buffer impacts.

edges.mechanism: Tourism disruption cuts local business revenue.

evidence.basis: Tourism disruption cutting local business revenue documented in regional economic-impact practice.
evidence.limitations: The tourism share of the local economy varies.

edges.mechanism: Industrial disruption propagates to suppliers and customers.

evidence.basis: Industrial disruption propagating to suppliers and customers documented in supply-chain management practice.
evidence.limitations: Supply-chain redundancy differs by sector.
